# Foldex DX12 startup and resize patch

This is the published, pinned wgpu-hal 30.0.1 crate from the local Cargo registry. Upstream licenses are retained. Five source files are patched: src/dx12/instance.rs, src/dx12/mod.rs, src/dx12/dcomp.rs, src/dx12/device.rs and src/auxil/dxgi/factory.rs. The optional APIs support preference-ordered discovery, composition presentation and benchmark timing. Other applications retain default HWND presentation.

DX12 upstream eagerly creates probe devices for all exposed adapters; egui-wgpu also retains the available adapter inventory for the render state's lifetime. GPU stage measurements identified discovery as the main startup cost, and full-window comparisons identified substantial unused-adapter retention. Existing public APIs cannot avoid the eager exposure boundary.

Foldex opts in only when DX12 is its sole enabled requested backend. The configured WGPU power preference is passed to Windows' IDXGIFactory6::EnumAdapterByGpuPreference, and the first supported adapter is exposed. This chooses from current hardware on each launch, without a stored hardware identifier. Older factories, enumeration errors and unsupported adapters fall back to upstream discovery. Existing Haswell/integrated-WARP exclusion rules remain. WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME bypasses this optimization and retains the full inventory for explicit selection. This adapter-discovery change does not alter shaders, allocations, validation or device limits.

Foldex now defaults to `DxgiFromVisual` and no-redirection HWNDs. The standard `WGPU_DX12_PRESENTATION_SYSTEM=Hwnd` override retains upstream HWND stretch behavior; `FOLDEX_DX12_RESIZE_SCALING=none` is a separate HWND diagnostic. Neither HWND scaling policy is the normal resize solution: physical interactive resizing still exposed gaps, while stretch resampled text.

The opted-in composition path keeps the UI swapchain matrix at identity (set and read back), with no scale or dynamic clip on the content visual. An untransformed container owns a separate background visual and content visual; explicit `AddVisual(content, true, background)` orders content above its sibling. Only the background is scaled, once, to cover the Win32 WM_SIZE pixel range, with nearest-neighbor sampling and hard edges. HWND clipping supplies visible bounds without resize-dependent composition commits.

`set_composition_windows` opts into this backdrop/publication policy independently of HWND diagnostics. A 1-by-1 BGRA8 UNORM composition swapchain is filled once per theme color using the existing D3D12 device/queue, normalized sRGB bytes, and a GPU fence before releasing temporary command resources. It has no repaint loop. On an upload-completion failure the error propagates; live-device resources whose completion cannot be established are quarantined rather than freed while in use. Library ownership remains alive with raw D3D12 references. Auto is explicitly normalized to DXGI_ALPHA_MODE_IGNORE in this path, because the shared converter otherwise maps it to UNSPECIFIED; both Auto and Opaque receive the backdrop. Premultiplied/postmultiplied surfaces retain transparency.

Content and the already-filled backdrop are first bound after a successful UI Present. Ordinary frames and in-place resizes retain the tree and issue no Commit. The backdrop covers a temporarily smaller last frame without stretching its UI or exposing the desktop; this does not claim atomic HWND/DXGI synchronization. UI VSync remains unchanged. `set_window_background_color` updates theme color without changing presentation policies. `last_window_presentation_target` reports the actual configured target (1 means HWND DirectComposition), and `last_window_scaling` reads the actual descriptor for HWND and composition chains. Composition's required stretch descriptor must not be confused with HWND image scaling. The existing raw swapchain accessor permits independent matrix verification. Physical interactive validation remains required.

For opted-in HWND composition with FIFO, successful swapchain configuration now marks the first UI presentation for `DXGI_PRESENT_RESTART`, retaining interval 1 and clearing the pending bit only after native Present succeeds. This discards queued presentations based on old geometry; no second present, DwmFlush, tearing policy change, or visual transform is introduced. Other surface targets and presentation modes retain their flags. This pairs with Foldex/eframe's scoped early `WM_NCCALCSIZE` paint. RESTART alone did not eliminate fixed-right-edge motion in the independent native marker probe, so the combined path requires displayed-window validation. See the open [wgpu #10548](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/10548) experiment and [Microsoft's DXGI_PRESENT reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/dxgi-present).

`last_composition_window_present` records the current thread's last successfully presented and published opted-in HWND composition frame: HWND, physical extent and a serial. It has no clock reads or allocations, and excludes the background's direct swapchain presentation. The native frame compares it across synchronous WM_PAINT so an egui-wgpu surface failure or deferred paint cannot falsely acknowledge an early frame and suppress the subsequent WM_SIZE fallback. It proves successful API completion, not when DWM displayed the frame.

The independent `set_pixel_preserving_windows` API remains available for explicit diagnostics with `FOLDEX_DX12_RESIZE_SCALING=none`; it is disabled by default, including when the variable is absent or invalid. Composition surfaces always retain upstream stretch behavior. `last_window_scaling()` reads back the actual swapchain descriptor for benchmark verification, rather than assuming the requested mode was accepted. The diagnostic opt-in does not establish that unscaled presentation is suitable for live resizing.

See [Microsoft's DXGI_SCALING definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgi1_2/ne-dxgi1_2-dxgi_scaling). The native resize benchmark records first-row text/icon geometry across 384 edge/corner size changes. That checks application geometry and actual swapchain configuration; it does not measure compositor presentation.

Diagnostics can override the preference with FOLDEX_DX12_SINGLE_ADAPTER=high|low|off. A separate benchmark-only FOLDEX_DX12_PREFERRED_ADAPTER_LUID=16hex path remains for the initial same-adapter comparison; invalid, stale or unsupported LUIDs retain upstream discovery. It is never set by the app and no hint file is written. The diagnostic GPU probe reports selected LUID and holds its HAL guard while making only read-only GetDesc2 calls.

Registry source provenance and modified paths are recorded in benchmarks/2026-10-21/p25-vendored-hal-provenance.json and the final provenance report. About 2.3MB of source is vendored, with no additional runtime service. The source patch should be re-reviewed when upgrading WGPU.

The independent `set_window_timings` diagnostic is enabled only by Foldex's opt-in stress mode. It accumulates elapsed nanoseconds for texture acquisition, queue submission, presentation, the nested frame-latency wait, and device fence waits. `take_window_timings` resets those counters and returns them with a cumulative presentation-call serial. The latency wait is a subspan of acquisition and must not be added to it. Measurements are process-global for the benchmark's single root window; they are API wall times, not GPU execution or displayed-frame timestamps. With diagnostics disabled, there are no clock reads or counter allocations. No wait durations, synchronization or presentation behavior are modified.

This probe exists because the pinned egui-wgpu painter subtracts acquisition, submission and presentation wall time from the renderer CPU figure that eframe reports. A small renderer CPU sample does not rule out a long graphics wait. Foldex's per-callback trace correlates these counters with callback intervals and raw input/UI stage times.
